newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds says preference is for acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds says preference is for acquisitions.

text.p: Lloyds TSB Group Plc chairman Sir Brian Pitman said on Friday that the bank's preference in dealing with surplus capital was to make more acquisitions to improve its competitive position.
But Pitman said that this would not be done unless it would improve shareholder value, adding that alternatives were to buy back shares or pay larger dividends.

"Our preference is to make more acquisitions to improve the bank's competitive position," Pitman told reporters at a news conference. "But we will not do so unless this would improve value to shareholders."
Pitman said that the bank had retained just over 800 million stg in the first half of 1997.
Asked to be more specific on acquisitions, Pitman would only say that there were some possibilities but refused to name them.
He said any acquisition would have to be fairly sizeable to be worth doing.
"We're not going to buy a company that will add 25 million to our profits. It's just not worth the bother," he said.
Asked if Lloyds would consider buying into investment banking, Pitman said, "Not a hope, I wouldn't touch it with a barge pole."
Pitman said, "If we can't do an acquisition, we will distribute the surplus -- we have to decide which is the most effective -- a buyback of shares, or bigger dividends."
